reader.requirement: At --std 85 the computer-name of the (Segmentation-module) OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph must be a system-name: a COBOL word of at most 30 characters drawn from A-Z (lowercase equivalent), 0-9 and '-', the hyphen neither first nor last, not a 1985 reserved word, otherwise formed as the implementor defines; and in this edition the clauses (MEMORY SIZE, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, SEGMENT-LIMIT) hang off a required computer-name.

edition-consulted.switches: word length ceiling: 30 below 2002, 31 at 2002/2014, 63 at 2023 (COBOL1567)
underscore in a COBOL word gated by ConstructRegistry user-word-underscore-2002 (COBOL0900 at 85); hyphen first/last refused at every edition (COBOL2773)
per-edition reserved-word list: a word reserved only from 2002 (TYPEDEF) is retyped to IDENTIFIER and accepted as a computer-name at 85, refused at 2023
computer-name-optional-2002: an OBJECT-COMPUTER clause without computer-name refused at 85 (COBOL0900)
SEGMENT-LIMIT accepted at 85, COBOL0902 removed at 2002+ (observed at --std 2023)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the name is capped at 30 characters, may not contain '_', may be a word 2002 reserved, and is required before any clause; at 2023 the cap is 63, '_' is allowed, 2002+ reserved words are refused, the name is optional, and SEGMENT-LIMIT is refused

reader.notes: computerName is cobolWord, so a 1985 reserved word never parses there while a word reserved only from 2002 is freed at 85 by the reservation gate; the lexer's word screens enforce the 1985 character set, the hyphen placement and the 30-character limit per edition. The only formation restriction beyond the 1985 text (no all-digit name) is implementor latitude the text grants and docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-198.md records.

refuter.evidence: Class c, words reserved only from 2002 used as the computer-name at --std 85 (r6n_<word>.cob: 'OBJECT-COMPUTER. <word>.'): 46 of 49 compile and run OK (TYPEDEF-like freeing works: ACTIVE-CLASS, BASED, FACTORY, INTERFACE, METHOD-ID, NULL, OBJECT, ...), but CLASS-ID and INTERFACE-ID are refused 'error COBOL5506: unexpected PROCEDURE ... expected a user-defined word', FUNCTION-ID is refused COBOL5506 at PROCEDURE, and REPOSITORY is refused COBOL3734 ('the paragraph header REPOSITORY follows other text of its line'); r6q 'OBJECT-COMPUTER. CLASS-ID SEGMENT-LIMIT IS 10.' refused COBOL0001. None of these words is in the 1985 text (grep of specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md finds CLASS-ID/FUNCTION-ID/REPOSITORY nowhere but FUNCTION-IDENTIFIER), and the compiler itself treats CLASS-ID as free at 85: r6r '01 CLASS-ID PIC X' compiles and prints 'OK A'. The 1985 text leaves formation to the implementor ('OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2  (4.2.2.1.2 System-Names)  the text is in the clause'), and the implementor's documented rule (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-198.md) is 'any COBOL word of the target edition ... with ONE added restriction: a system-name shall not consist of digits only', so these are legal computer-names that the compiler refuses. Cause: CobolParserCore.g4#computerName is 'cobolWord' only (no reservedGatedWord), and the optional computerName in objectComputerParagraph lets the parser end the paragraph and read CLASS-ID / INTERFACE-ID / FUNCTION-ID / REPOSITORY as a new unit or paragraph header, so no syntax error lands on the free word and ReservationGateRewriter never retypes it. 1985 reserved words are all refused (22 probed: ALTER, CD, RERUN, TAPE, DEBUG-ITEM, ...), as the reader found. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XVI.2.2.3 SR1  (║2.2.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR1'. kb/Work grep for computer-name with these words: none.
